question: Does a directly addressed four-level checkpoint ladder let the iterative half-memory attacker avoid enough repeated work to complete a canonical proof under the same byte and operation ceilings?

independent_strategy.difference_from_prior_policy: replace one twelve-entry linear-scanned checkpoint table with four independently addressed time scales totaling sixty-four entries
independent_strategy.lookup: probe exactly one target-word-derived slot in each level, charge all four probes, validate the stored bundle, and resume from the greatest valid stop below the request
independent_strategy.capture: after a replayed iteration, write the target-aware four-value bundle into every level whose stride divides the new stop; these bounded writes are part of the already charged replay iteration

charged_operations: every memo get or put probe
each of four directly addressed checkpoint-level probes
operation_policy.invariant: total_operations equals logical_value_requests plus replay_iterations plus memo_probes plus checkpoint_probes
operation_policy.failure: refuse before an operation that would exceed the ceiling and emit no proof

selected_configuration.primary_allocation: 1/128 of possible 16-byte primary slots after allocator reserve

holdout_policy.selection_rule: No parameter changes after any holdout result is observed; retain all eight rows, including unfavorable outcomes.

gate_mapping.reason: The screen must first establish exact independent boundaries. A gate assessment still requires canonical proofs, total measured attack memory on controlled hosts, and independent review.
